why: The picture shows one walled compound with roofs over the whole outline; the inner outline is a part of it. One shell is enough: the inner one would only hide inside the outer one
The picture shows a ring building with an open court; the inner outline is that court. Shells have no holes yet, so the outer outline stands alone and the inner one goes
The inner outline is a small core inside one building in a wooded plot: the outer outline already covers it
The inner outline is the link block between two long wings that the outer outline already covers
The picture shows a courtyard house: the inner outline is its court, covered by the outer outline in the stand-in world
The picture shows a very large ribbed roof, an exhibition hall of Pragati Maidan: 29.1 m is right for a hall of this span, the 2 levels are its floors
The same exhibition hall complex at Pragati Maidan (a wide ribbed roof with a road passing under it): the tall height is right
The oval ribbed roof of the Pragati Maidan hall: a hall of this size is about 29 m high, the height tag stays
The stub is the corner of a small drive loop beside the building and points into its wall: nothing to drive to, it goes
The stub hangs off a bend of the service road under trees with no drive or gate beyond it in the picture: a drawing slip, it goes
The end stops on paved ground at the corner of the lane ahead with nothing between them in the picture: one junction
The service road runs up to the road ahead through open ground; no wall or gate shows between them
The lane runs along the building straight to the junction of lanes ahead: it joins there
Two drives of one compound under the trees, the end in line with the bend ahead: one drive drawn with a gap
The drive runs along the top of the lawn to the lane at its west edge: it meets the lane
Two ends face each other across 12 m of tree cover on one line: one lane drawn with a gap
